scan_notes: Reviewed the exact abbb8e4f..3bcddf31 diff; the worktree HEAD is later, so all line evidence below is from the 3bcddf31 blobs. Read the data, testing, security, instruction, and least-privilege guidance; ran scripts/fact_check.py --commit 3bcddf31 (PASS); traced init_db, db.pg autocommit behavior, torque_app provisioning, all is_real readers, the new tests, and every remaining _REAL_PRODUCTS occurrence. Sequential behavior is correct: fresh/prod write only the marker, dev updates the three rows, later sequential boots skip, and an operator promotion survives. The UPDATE and COMMENT are atomic because the DO block is one PostgreSQL statement/transaction. The documented torque_app provisioning reassigns ownership to torque_app, so COMMENT is permitted; if the live role truly does not own clients, earlier ALTER TABLE statements already abort init_db before this block. Quoting and consistent unqualified/regclass resolution are sound. Readers are also coherent: client_registry and review queue require == 1, the workbook filters on tenant realness, and page_resolution intentionally continues serving non-demo canaries. The four stated mutations are constrained, but the one-shot test admits a weaker row-state sentinel described below. Most residual _REAL_PRODUCTS references are dated, SHA-anchored, historical, or explicitly superseded; two still issue live instructions.

findings.title: Concurrent first boots can reapply the one-shot backfill
findings.evidence: The block begins directly with `IF NOT EXISTS (...) THEN` and then performs the UPDATE and COMMENT, with no lock serializing concurrent first executions.
findings.failure_scenario: During the first rolling deployment, task A and task B both enter the DO block before either marker is committed. A finishes and an operator then promotes `silver_canary` to 1, while B is paused between its guard and UPDATE. B resumes and writes the row back to 0 despite the marker now existing.
findings.suggested_fix: Acquire a migration-specific `pg_advisory_xact_lock` before evaluating the guard, so a waiting task rechecks the marker after the first transaction commits.

findings.title: The one-shot test accepts a row-state sentinel as its guard
findings.evidence: The test promotes only `silver_canary`, then explicitly requires the other two rows to remain 0: `assert after["browser_drill_co"] == 0 and after["tor682_canary"] == 0`. It never asserts that the pg_description marker exists.
findings.failure_scenario: Replace the comment guard with `IF no named canary currently has is_real = 0`. Every test passes: the first run applies, and after the test promotes one row the other two zero rows suppress later runs. In production, promoting all three removes that sentinel, and the next boot demotes all three again.
findings.suggested_fix: Assert the marker exists after the first boot, and promote all three canaries before subsequent boots so no row value can act as the one-shot marker.

findings.title: The red-team prompt names a nonexistent tenant subcommand
findings.evidence: The new instruction says: ``torque-admin tenant create``. At this revision, scripts/torque_admin.py defines tenant subcommands `add`, `list`, and `update`; only the separate `client` group has `create`.
findings.failure_scenario: A worker follows the prompt to register SMPRT and runs `torque-admin tenant create ...`; argparse rejects the command, so the prescribed registration workflow cannot be completed.

findings.title: An active plan still recommends deriving demos from the dead literal
findings.evidence: Outside the code fences, the plan still says: `Its demo set is DERIVED (_REGISTRY product codes minus _REAL_PRODUCTS)` and `Prefer this to the _DEMO_CODES literal above if that pin holds at build time; verify it.`
findings.failure_scenario: An agent following this implementation plan recreates the subtraction using the current database-backed real set. On an empty database or failed registry read, every registered product becomes a demo, silently labelling real-client products simulated. The cited `_REAL_PRODUCTS` equality pin no longer exists to prevent it.
findings.suggested_fix: Strike this recommendation and state that the shipped `_DEMO_CODES` declaration is intentional; keep the historical text clearly marked as rejected.

findings.title: A required falsifier still depends on the deleted symbol
findings.evidence: Under `Cheap checks ... Run them before executing`, item 6 says: `_REAL_PRODUCTS returns 6` even though the symbol was deleted.
findings.failure_scenario: A worker runs the required pre-execution checks, finds no `_REAL_PRODUCTS`, and has no defined branch distinguishing “six products” from “the check is obsolete.” The worker can proceed with the stale 15-page denominator without the advertised falsifier ever deciding it.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the check with an explicit query of `clients WHERE is_real = 1` for the target database, or the named per-codebase oracle where that is the intended population.

findings.title: Workbook provenance omits product-specific served slots
findings.evidence: The new source table says `clients (is_real) x companies._SLOTS` defines the served population. The implementation calls `served_slots(code)`, which includes both `_SLOTS` and matching `_PRODUCT_SLOTS`.
findings.failure_scenario: A maintainer reconstructing or refactoring the population from this source table uses only `_SLOTS` and silently drops ALM's product-specific Deal Ops slots from the workbook and sprint denominator.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the source entry to `clients (is_real) x served_slots(code)`.

findings.title: Migration rationale omits the actual update writer
findings.evidence: The comment says `api/services/vault/clients.py is the only production writer of this column`, but `api/services/control_plane/tenants.py::update_tenant` writes `changes["is_real"]` and is the operator path discussed immediately above.
findings.failure_scenario: A future audit follows the claimed single writer and changes only vault/clients.py, overlooking the supported tenant-update path that can alter realness.
findings.suggested_fix: Name both writers and narrow the relevant claim to neither writer issuing COMMENT statements.

findings.title: Migration comment gives invalid tenant-update syntax
findings.evidence: The comment gives ``torque-admin tenant update <slug> --real``. The parser requires `tenant update --slug <slug> --real`; the slug is not positional.
findings.failure_scenario: An operator copies the documented command while correcting a canary and argparse rejects the positional slug, leaving the row unchanged.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `torque-admin tenant update --slug <slug> --real` here and in the matching test docstring.

overall_explanation: The SQL is correct for every sequential boot state and is atomic under autocommit, permissions are valid under the repository's documented ownership model, and the four named readers do not count the backfilled canaries as real. However, the first-rollout guard is not serialized, the test suite permits a materially weaker row-state guard, and the citation sweep leaves two actionable `_REAL_PRODUCTS` instructions plus an invalid tenant-registration command. The latter are realistic wrong-behavior paths, so the reviewed commit is not sound.
